baslik: Why Glass Explodes for No Reason
aciklama:
Some glass can explode by itself, days after it is installed. Here is the hidden flaw.

#shorts #science #engineering #howitworks #glass

sahneler.metin: Some glass can explode all by itself, with no impact.
The whole panel bursts into thousands of pieces at once.
And it's not weak glass. It's the tough, tempered kind.
It's cooled fast, so the surface is squeezed while the core is stretched.
A microscopic impurity inside can slowly grow.
When it reaches the stretched core, all that energy releases.
It can happen years after the glass was made.

vaka.mekanizma: an inclusion growing into the tensioned core
vaka.ders: glass for high-rise facades can be heat-soak tested
vaka.yanilgi: 'Spontaneous' breakage isn't random — a tiny nickel sulfide inclusion can slowly expand until it cracks the stressed core.
vaka.tartisma: Should skyscraper glass always be heat-soak tested to find these flaws before installation?
